correctness.rationale: All 4-subsets are facets of rank4 by four-neighborliness, and 8-facets of even-dimensional cyclic C(n,8) are unions of four disjoint edges of cycle C_n by Gale evenness. D4 is 1-dimensional (no 12-vertex facets), with V=C(n,4), #facets F_n=n(n−5)(n−6)(n−7)/24 and E=35F_n (unique 8-union per edge). For path-edge subgraph H_n, complementary 4-subsets preserve the three parity classes j=0,1,2. I checked the written induction: n=10 finite base has 210 vertices/15 path facets/525 edges, component sizes 10,100,100. For any new T containing last label, use forced last path edge and cover at most 3 other marked vertices by 3 disjoint edges in an N=n−2>=9 path; if N odd, at least one unmarked even-indexed vertex can be omitted, leaving perfectly matched even paths. Thus every new vertex connects to old same-j component. Even-n closing edge preserves parity and no classes merge. Odd-n wrap edge connects 4→1 and 3→2 parity-count types and merges all three H_n classes; n=9 KG(9,4) connected via one-vertex exchanges. For even n, each facet has four even/four odd and contributes respectively 1,16,18 distinct edges to classes, giving E_j and the stated ranks. Independent regeneration for n9..17 checked F_n, edge counts, parity components and betti ranks; finite examples are only a cross-check, not the proof for all n.
residual_risks: Exact finite checks do not generalize outside the claim domain.

value.rationale: The boundary of the neighborly cyclic eight-polytope is a canonical simplicial seven-sphere. Its four-tupling, a natural extension of the recently introduced double, exhibits an exact odd/even connectivity phase transition and three distinct parity-complement components; four is the first tuple size admitting three complement-invariant classes. Uniform formulas for all integral first-homology circle ranks and a constructive parity mechanism make this a substantive structural theorem, not a finite tabulation.
residual_risks: Motivated but scope-limited finding; not evidence of stronger generalization.
